newsitem.title: USA: Ill. unemployment falls to 4.4 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Ill. unemployment falls to 4.4 pct in May.

text.p: Illinois' seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped from 4.8 percent in April to 4.4 percent in May, Illinois Department of Employment Security announced Tuesday.
"The May statistics confirm that the Illinois economy continues on its longrunning healthy course," department Director Lynn Doherty said in a statement.
The unemployment rate in April had dropped to its lowest point since 1974 and the May statistics show that Illinois unemployment has remained below national levels for seven consecutive months.
The national rate for May was 4.8 percent and the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for May 1996 was 5.3 percent.
Non-farm payroll jobs rose 67,300 from May 1996 until May 1997, with the services sector posting the largest gain of 62 percent on an increase of 41,800 jobs, according to the department.
